evals.prompt: What's breaking on trtllm main right now? Give me a rundown with root causes.
evals.expected_output: A saved markdown report on recent (7d) Main Break detections from the trtllm-infra stability report, with real entity names/platforms/links and grounded root-cause hypotheses, plus a chat summary.
assertions: Output cites at least 3 real, specific test/stage entity names (not generic placeholders) that plausibly come from the trtllm-infra Detection Details data
Output states or implies a time window (e.g. last 7 days) consistent with the dashboard's Main Break detection window
Output distinguishes confidence/severity levels or otherwise ranks failures by importance rather than listing them all as equally urgent
Output offers a root-cause hypothesis (regression / flaky / infra) per notable failure, not just a bare list of failing tests
Output includes at least one working reference link (Jenkins, test history, or NVDF document URL) back to the source data
A markdown report file was saved to disk, not just printed in chat

evals.prompt: Pull the last 7 days of main break detections from the stability report and summarize the worst ones.
evals.expected_output: Same as above, focused on top offenders by confidence/failure count.
assertions: Output ranks/orders failures by severity (e.g. confidence, failure count, PR count) rather than an arbitrary or alphabetical list
Output cites real, specific entity names and platforms from the data, not placeholders
Output quantifies failures with real numbers (failure count, pass count, or PR count) pulled from the data
A markdown report file was saved to disk

evals.prompt: Is DGX_B200 having more CI trouble than other platforms on trtllm main this week?
evals.expected_output: An analysis grounded in real per-platform failure counts from the fetched data, answering the comparative question.
assertions: Output gives a direct yes/no/inconclusive answer to the comparative question
Output backs the answer with real per-platform counts (e.g. number of Main Break groups or failures on DGX_B200 vs. other platforms), not a vague impression
Output names at least one specific platform other than DGX_B200 for comparison
Output does not fabricate platform names or numbers not derivable from the fetched data
